outputs.summary:
Deterministic, resumable, bounded generation over the pinned FWGC++ producer, in the C++ worldbridge.

- Canonical JSON: mnbl.canonical-json/1 = RFC 8785 (cjson; independently checked against JavaScript on 300k numbers and 400 documents).
- Identities:
  - RequestId = sha256("mnbl.request-id/1 mnbl.canonical-json/1\n" + canonical request).
  - ConfigurationId has the same form, excluding the instance and seedSource fields.
  - SourceInputId = lock + binary + recipe hash.
  - WorldContentId = a sorted path/size/sha256 inventory; links of every kind are refused.
- Request validation: strict schema; seed 0..4294967295, verified against the pinned binary and recorded in worldgen/contracts/producer-seed-width.json; override numbers within 2^53 under any spelling.
- Attempt schedule (mnbl.retry-seed/1):
  - Only declared world-quality codes are retried, up to the bound product policy's maxQualityAttempts; input, mechanical, parser and engine failures end the generation.
  - The state is persisted after every transition: durable write-through rename, exclusive state lock, per-attempt run history, strict load (seeds must re-derive, status must be consistent).
  - Cancel and hard kill resume with the same seed.
  - Accepted, exhausted and failed states are frozen; an accepted world is re-verified by WorldContentId.
- CLI:
  - worldbridge --new-request: requires the three policies and the attempt ceiling; never overwrites an existing request.
  - worldbridge --generate: takes its quality gate, source contract and ceiling only from the request-bound policies. Attempt dirs are request-scoped and created exclusively, so a collision is refused (work_collision) and an existing dir is never adopted.
  - UTF-8 paths throughout. A --work path the ANSI code page cannot spell is refused before any state exists (producer argv limit).
- Two independent reviews: the first found 2 blocking and 15 other defects; the re-review found no blocking defects. The low-severity follow-ups (A-D, plus E's error format) are fixed and covered by evidence.

Not done / residual:
- WorldContentId covers producer output only; no compiler exists yet.
- Recovering a deleted state with existing work dirs costs one work_collision (exit 2, retryable JSON) per previously run attempt.
- The seed-width record is a self-declared file tied only to the producer sha256.
- Empty directories do not affect WorldContentId.
- The `engine` failure class is exercised only by the scripted runner.

Sampling:

Static travel graph and port candidate compiler (worldbridge --compile-travel) on the MMR-26 compiled terrain, under the MMR-17 War Sails contract (worldgen/calibration/naval-transitions) and a versioned playability policy. Everything is a static candidate with status pendingEngineValidation, plus mandatory host checks for MMR-38.

Cells: the compiled grid's cells, classified as sea, lake, river, land or mountain by the MMR-17/18 fixture rules, with the proposed TerrainType per class checked against the engine's invalid sets. Connectivity is through shared edges only, wrapping across the seam.

Repairs: road passes, settlement footprints with access passes, snaps and harbour shifts. Each is deterministic, bounded and recorded with stable UIDs; a bound overrun rejects the world with the UIDs.

Roads: decoded to town UIDs and rasterized into lattice paths. Crossings are classified as river, lake, coast or blocked. River and lake runs of at most 2 cells are bridge candidates that join land groups; coast never joins. Every producer river crossing gets an outcome.

Basins: open or closed, with OpenSea flags.

Ports: only from producer harbour records on open basins. A port serves its gate: the coast pair of the gate's land component nearest the gate, never shared, and within 2 cells of the gate (the installed War Sails port-gate envelope, max 10.97 units).

Transitions and reachability: port and coast transitions. Player reachability follows MMR-17: the player embarks at a port and disembarks on any coast; a group is player-safe when it can be reached and left.

Outcomes: an unreachable or unplaceable town rejects the world. Villages outside their town's land group, and castles that are not player-safe, are excluded within bounds.

Outputs: travel-graph.json, ports.json, cells.bin, and campaign.json (the MMR-27 records after the exclusions, with the MMR-28 position and portSite slots resolved).

FWG-03: worldbridge --generate runs this gate on every attempt when a request binds playability and the compiler policies. The 4 quality codes are retryable; reasons carry UIDs and each attempt keeps its travel outputs.

outputs.summary:
CampaignGraphValidator (pure managed) validates a whole staged campaign graph before it registers, and owns full reference closure and the unexpected-Calradia census. Diagnostics are aggregated (code, source UID, generated id, property path, reason), so one run reports every failure.

What it checks:
- Input shape.
- Registered types, duplicate ids, unknown objects.
- Unexpected Calradia instances, including the characters of installed heroes.
- Transitive reference closure: through installed templates, live defaults and optional (loader-tolerated) references; aliases count only when staged.
- Reference types per property.
- Ownership: ruler, ruling clan, capital, clan leaders, fief owners.
- Hero roles: character, clan, Lord occupation.
- Settlement components and location complexes; village bindings (markets).
- Ports and shipyards.
- Troop upgrade cycles over every staged or reached character.
- Initial-party intent: clan homes, bandit homes, runtime notables and companions, relations.
- Calradia coordinates: settlements, start points and spawn positions.
